content:
Sam: :rotating_light: Pager — Dedicated us-central1 cluster (dc-cedar-01) showing elevated token latency and 502/504s starting ~1888004300. Network error patterns in infra logs. Paging @Priya (oncall) and @Diego (infra).

Priya: on it. I see the same — spike in RTTs from inference nodes to TPU‑backed shims, lots of TCP retransmits. Repro: curl against internal health endpoint returns 504 intermittently. Starting live mitigation checklist.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2387 — Priority: SEV-2 — Channel: #vendors — Owner: Priya — Pager fired at 1888004321

Diego: Can someone paste the exact error lines from router logs? I want sample connection traces + flow logs to correlate with BGP events.

Sam: pasted below (tail of router logs):
```
[1888004305] tcp retransmit from 10.12.3.5 -> 10.12.8.7 seq=... rst? timeout
[1888004310] upstream=10.12.8.7 status=504 latency=1200ms
[1888004320] connection reset by peer
```

Elena (CS): Heads up — two Dedicated customers in us-central (AcmeHealth, FinGraph) opened support tickets citing timeouts on embeddings endpoints. We should prepare a customer note + targeted DM.

Priya: Diego, can you confirm if this is regional (us-central) only? Any load balancer / platform config change in the last 2 hours?

Diego: No config deploys from our side in last 3 hours. Metric correlation shows loss of BFD keepalives between our peering and GCP's us-central egress. Suspecting upstream network flapping. I'm escalating to GCP via our TAM and opening a formal ticket.

Sam: > I called TAM. GCP acknowledged an internal issue flagged under PSN-59214. They say it's affecting some VPC egress in us-central for the last ~30m. Asking for ETA.

GCP Support: Hi team — we have an engineering investigation ongoing. Root cause suspected in a transit router cluster. We're escalating to networking eng. Patch ETA unknown. I'll post updates in this thread and in the PSN ticket.

Priya: OK — we need immediate mitigations: 1) failover traffic to us-west (if allowed for these customers), 2) reroute any cross-region requests, 3) update status page + send proactive customer notifications to affected Dedicated tenants. Who can run the failover?

Sam: I can coordinate failover for non-sensitive tenants with autoswitch. For Dedicated customers we need opt-in; Elena can DM customers with instructions and offer temporary route to our standby region.

Elena (CS): Preparing DM template. Question: do we have a safe SSH/DB maintenance window for AcmeHealth? They have strict SLAs.

Priya: Not yet. Diego—do we have warm capacity in us-west? How fast to spin up inference groups and resync KV caches?

Diego: Warm pools are available but cold start for large models is ~8–12min. KV cache repopulation depends on prefix cache and customer traffic. For immediate impact reduction, we can route new sessions to us-west and keep existing in us-central — reduces churn. I'll start a canary failover for one low-impact tenant.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder — Priya to Diego at 1888004450 for second shift.

Sam: Drafting status page update — please review:

"Update 1888004360: We are investigating increased latency and intermittent timeouts for Redwood Dedicated customers in us-central (affecting embeddings & generation). Root cause appears to be an upstream networking issue reported by our cloud provider. Engineers are working with the provider and implementing traffic failover where possible. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes or as new info becomes available. Impact: elevated latency, intermittent 502/504 errors for a subset of traffic."

Priya: Shorter: "We are investigating degraded inference performance in us-central due to an upstream cloud networking issue. Some requests may see elevated latency or errors. Engineers are working with the provider to mitigate."

Elena (CS): Customer DM template (short):

"Hi [Name], we're investigating intermittent timeouts and higher latency for Redwood Dedicated clusters in us‑central. Our engineering team is coordinating with our cloud provider and implementing mitigations (regional failover). We'll notify you when traffic has been routed or service restored. If you want us to opt your cluster into the failover now, reply YES and we'll proceed. — Elena, Customer Success"

Sam: Added note to status page draft: include affected resource IDs: dc-cedar-01, dc-cedar-02, lb-us-central-01. Also link to PSN ticket: https://gcp.example/psn/PSN-59214 (internal link)

GCP Support: Update: PSN-59214 — an edge router cluster in us-central sees packet loss due to a software rollback failure. We have a hotfix in validation and expect staged rollout in ~25-40 minutes. We'll provide incremental updates.

Priya: Ok good. Action log:
- [ ] Post status page update (Sam)
- [ ] Send targeted Customer DMs (Elena)
- [ ] Start canary failover for non-compliant tenants (Sam)
- [ ] Open temporary routing for opt-in Dedicated clusters (Diego)
- [ ] Monitor error rates & token costs (Riley)

Riley (ops): Monitoring dashboards show errors trending down slightly since 1888004410 after initial routing tweaks. Token cost spiked due to retries — tracking with alerts.

Elena (CS): DM sent to AcmeHealth & FinGraph. AcmeHealth replied YES — want failover. FinGraph asked for ETA before switching.

Diego: Kicked off opt-in reroute for AcmeHealth at 1888004520 — new sessions should hit us-west LB. Routing rules updated: priority-based policy to prefer us-west when peering latency > 200ms.

Sam: Posting status page now.

Sam: statuspage API call:
```
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/components/us-central/incidents \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API" \
 -d '{"status":"investigating","message":"Investigating degraded inference in us-central due to upstream cloud network issue. Some customers may experience latency or errors. Updates every 15 minutes."}'
```

oncall-bot: Status page updated by Sam at 1888004530 — link https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-2387

Priya: GCP update: rolling hotfix started at 1888004555; they expect progressive rollouts across nodes. Keep monitoring; if we see stable RTTs for 10m post-rollout, we can start failback plan.

Riley: Error volume down 37% since reroute. Latency median still elevated for a subset. Token retry budget high; throttling applied to low-priority background jobs.

Elena (CS): FinGraph replied to DM — wants to wait 20 mins for GCP update. Not switching yet.

GCP Support: Hotfix validation shows good results on first wave. ETA for full remediation ~30mins. We're keeping this ticket open and will escalate if rollback symptoms reappear.

Priya: Good. I'm taking a short break — Diego will be lead for next 30m. Diego please ensure we keep customers informed and update status page after next GCP note.

Diego: Taking lead. Posting internal comms template for legal/proc: "Affected customers: list; incident start: 1888004300; impact: elevated latency and intermittent 5xx for Dedicated in us‑central; mitigation: opt-in regional reroute + cloud vendor hotfix; next update: <time>" — can someone sign off?

Sam: LGTM. Add note: potential postmortem to include: root cause, timeline, why opt-in required for Dedicated, remediation steps for automated cross-region failover.

oncall-bot: Handoff logged: Priya -> Diego at 1888004450

GCP Support: All nodes in the cluster have rolled the hotfix by 1888004640. Monitoring indicates packet loss returned to baseline. We'll monitor for 15 minutes and close PSN when stable.

Riley: Observability shows latency baseline restored around 1888004650; error rate < 1% now. I'll mark monitoring green after 15m stable window.

Elena (CS): Messaging update to customers: "Service restored for most traffic in us‑central. Some customers who opted into regional failover are still on us-west; we'll coordinate failback when it's safe. If you still see errors after 15 minutes, please open a ticket and we'll prioritize." — sending now.

Sam: Adding post-incident tasks: schedule postmortem, outreach to top affected customers with timeline and credits, review failover opt-in flow for Dedicated (make it auto opt-in with safety guardrails?).

Priya: Back from break — thanks team. I'm going to create the incident postmortem doc and invite infra, product, CS, and our TAM.

GCP Support: Closing PSN-59214 in 90 minutes if no regressions. Contact your TAM for continuing questions. Glad we could help mitigate.

Sam: Closing thread summary: incident start 1888004300, vendor network transit issue, hotfix rolled, mitigations applied (opt-in reroute), most customers restored by 1888004650. Assigning postmortem owner: Priya. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Participants in this thread will be used for follow-up actions and review.
